title: Approximation for henselian pairs with a Noetherian G-ring
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] such that $A$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (in particular Noetherian), and let $A^\wedge$ be the $I$-adic completion of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and let $\hat a_1,\ldots,\hat a_n\in A^\wedge$ with $f_j^\iota(\hat a_1,\ldots,\hat a_n)=0$ for $j=1,\ldots,m$ ($f_j^\iota$: coefficients mapped by $\iota$). Then for every $N\ge1$ there are $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in A$ with $f_j(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=0$ for all $j$ and $\hat a_k-\iota(a_k)\in I^NA^\wedge$ for all $k$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair, line 3389), case (2); proof: (2) implies A -> A^ regular (More on Algebra, Lemma 0AH2, lemma-map-G-ring-to-completion-regular), Popescu theorem (Smoothing, Theorem 07GC) factors the solution through a smooth A-algebra, More on Algebra, Lemmas 07M7 (lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism) and 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair) give the solution in A; cited in pione.tex, proof of Lemma 0GS2, line 1833

proof.text: *Reduction to a regular completion map.* Fix $(A,I)$, $f_1,\ldots,f_m$, $\hat a_1,\ldots,\hat a_n$ and $N\ge1$ as in the statement. Since $A$ is a G-ring it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], so $I$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] the canonical map $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ is regular. (Stacks: '(2) implies (1)', so it suffices to treat the case $A\to A^\wedge$ regular.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair, line 3389), first paragraph: 'By More on Algebra, Lemma 0AH2 we see that (2) implies (1)'

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-polynomial-factorization] to the regular completion map obtained in step 1, the finite equations f, and ahat. Obtain a smooth A-algebra B, an A-algebra map ψ:B→A^, and b with f_j(b)=0 and ψ(b_k)=ahat_k. The cited theorem is proved by Popescu and the finite-presentation colimit factorization, exactly the previous step 2.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair, line 3389), second paragraph: 'By Theorem 07GC we can find a factorization A -> B -> A^ with A -> B smooth and b_1,...,b_n in B with f_j(b_1,...,b_n)=0 in B' (the source writes 'A -> P smooth', a misprint for A -> B); the factorization of the finitely presented C through a stage is Algebra 07C3 (1)=>(2) / 00QO

proof.text: *Lifting the section modulo $I^N$ to an etale $A$-algebra.* Let $\pi_N:A\to A/I^N$ be the quotient map and $\pi^\wedge_N:A^\wedge\to A/I^N$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto x_N$, the $A$-algebra map of [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Then $\sigma=\pi^\wedge_N\circ\psi:B\to A/I^N$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-section-etale-lift] applied to the ideal $J=I^N$ there are a ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale such that $\alpha:A/I^N\to A'/I^NA'$ is an isomorphism, and an $A$-algebra map $\tilde\sigma:B\to A'$ with $q\circ\tilde\sigma=\alpha\circ\sigma$, where $q:A'\to A'/I^NA'$ is the quotient map.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair, line 3389), third paragraph: 'Denote sigma: B -> A^ -> A/I^N the composition. By More on Algebra, Lemma 07M7 we can find an etale ring map A -> A' which induces an isomorphism A/I^N -> A'/I^NA' and an A-algebra map tilde sigma: B -> A' lifting sigma'

proof.text: The HenselianRing hypothesis gives I≤jacobson(0) directly by HenselianRing.jac. For a Gabber polynomial, reduction modulo I gives X^r(X−1), which has root 1 and derivative 1 at 1. Apply Mathlib HenselianRing.is_henselian to lift this simple root to β with β−1∈I. The private helper proves these reductions explicitly. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-root-criterion-etale-section-lifting] to the étale A-algebra A′ and the section A′→A/I induced by the inverse quotient isomorphism of step 3 followed by A/I^N→A/I. This gives χ:A′→A. Henselianity is only used for I, never asserted for I^N.

source.place: proof of Smoothing Lemma Tag 0AH5, 'Since (A, I) is henselian, there is an A-algebra map chi: A' -> A, see More on Algebra, Lemma 09XI'; here 09XI (1)=>(2) along the proof of More on Algebra Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553): (3)=>(1) [the DAG's definition is (3)], (1)=>(5) (the root argument written out here), (5)=>(2)

proof.text: *$\chi$ agrees with the section modulo $I^N$.* Claim: $\pi_N\circ\chi=\alpha^{-1}\circ q$ as maps $A'\to A/I^N$. Every $A$-algebra map $h:A'\to A/I^N$ kills $I^NA'$ (it sends $I^N$ to $0$), so $h=\bar h\circ q$ for an $A$-algebra map $\bar h:A'/I^NA'\to A/I^N$; then $\bar h\circ\alpha:A/I^N\to A/I^N$ is an $A$-algebra map, hence the identity ($A\to A/I^N$ is surjective), so $\bar h=\alpha^{-1}$ and $h=\alpha^{-1}\circ q$. Apply this to $h=\pi_N\circ\chi$ (an $A$-algebra map since $\chi$ is). Hence $\pi_N\circ\chi\circ\tilde\sigma=\alpha^{-1}\circ q\circ\tilde\sigma=\sigma$ (step 3).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair, line 3389), last sentence ('Then setting a_i = chi(tilde sigma(b_i)) gives a solution'), the congruence left implicit there, written out

proof.text: *The solution.* Put $a_k=\chi(\tilde\sigma(b_k))\in A$. Since $\chi\circ\tilde\sigma:B\to A$ is an $A$-algebra map, $f_j(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=\chi\tilde\sigma(f_j(b_1,\ldots,b_n))=0$ by step 2. By step 5 and step 2, $\pi_N(a_k)=\sigma(b_k)=\pi^\wedge_N(\psi(b_k))=\pi^\wedge_N(\hat a_k)$, and $\pi^\wedge_N\circ\iota=\pi_N$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], so $\pi^\wedge_N(\hat a_k-\iota(a_k))=0$. Since $I$ is finitely generated (step 1), the kernel of $\pi^\wedge_N$ is $I^NA^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], i.e. $\hat a_k-\iota(a_k)\in I^NA^\wedge$ for $k=1,\ldots,n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair, line 3389), last sentence: 'Then setting a_i = chi(tilde sigma(b_i)) gives a solution'; the congruence 'hat a_i - a_i in I^N' of the statement means I^N A^ (Algebra Lemma 05GG)

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Smoothing 0AH5 and its proof, More on Algebra 0AH2, 07M7, 09XI, Smoothing 07GC, Algebra 00QO, 07C3 and 05GG; all tags checked in tags/tags. Statement kept (it is case (2) of 0AH5; 'hat a_i - a_i in I^N' made precise as I^N A^). Proof in 6 steps following the source: (1) A Noetherian, A^ Noetherian, A -> A^ regular (new unsplit lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular, 0AH2); (2) the solution as an A-algebra map from C = A[x]/(f) to A^, factored through a smooth A-algebra B by Popescu (new unsplit lem-weil-pbc-popescu-smoothing, 07GC) and the factorization of finitely presented algebras through a stage of a filtered colimit (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit, 00QO/07C3, RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_eq_comp_ι_app_of_isColimit); (3) the section B -> A/I^N lifted to an etale A' with A/I^N = A'/I^NA' (new unsplit lem-weil-pbc-smooth-section-etale-lift, 07M7); (4) a retraction A' -> A from the henselian property, via the existing reviewed nodes lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion and lem-weil-pbc-gabber-root-criterion-etale-section-lifting (09XI (3)=>(1)=>(5)=>(2), the root step written out), since no node states 09XI (1)=>(2) directly; (5) the retraction agrees with the section mod I^N (uniqueness of A-algebra maps A' -> A/I^N, written out; the source leaves it implicit); (6) the solution and the congruence via the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power (05GG (2), AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval). Source misprint noted: 'A -> P smooth' for A -> B.
